notes: Historical facts: Revenue, Operating profit (EBIT proxy), Depreciation & amortization, and Additions to property, plant & equipment are taken directly from Conagra’s FY2025 annual report for fiscal years ended May 28, 2023; May 26, 2024; and May 25, 2025. ([conagrabrands.com](https://www.conagrabrands.com/files/2025-annual-report))

EBIT definition caveat: EBIT in this input is modeled using GAAP 'Operating profit' which includes non-cash impairment charges; base-case EBIT margin is therefore a normalized operating-margins assumption anchored to FY2026 adjusted operating margin guidance rather than directly to the volatile GAAP operating profit history. ([conagrabrands.com](https://www.conagrabrands.com/files/events/2025-12-19/Q2FY26-Earnings-Press-Release))

Tax rate base-case uses adjusted effective tax rate of 23.5% disclosed in Q2 FY26 guidance context (modeled as a steady tax_rate for the DCF). ([conagrabrands.com](https://www.conagrabrands.com/files/events/2025-12-19/Q2FY26-Earnings-Press-Release))

NWC construction (historical and carried into pct-of-sales) is calculated as: (Total current assets − cash & cash equivalents) − (Total current liabilities − notes payable − current installments of long-term debt). NWC includes 'current assets held for sale' and 'current liabilities held for sale' as part of total current assets/liabilities. ([conagrabrands.com](https://www.conagrabrands.com/files/2025-annual-report))
Capital intensity base-case uses historical D&A and capex intensity (as % of sales) and assumes mild normalization over the forecast window.

WACC (0.09) and terminal_growth (0.02) are modeling assumptions not explicitly provided in the cited filings/press releases; they are set to be economically conservative for a large-cap consumer staples/food company with material leverage. ([conagrabrands.com](https://www.conagrabrands.com/files/events/2025-12-19/Q2FY26-Earnings-Press-Release))

Terminal method is Gordon growth; terminal_exit_ebitda_multiple is set to null because it is not used under gordon_growth. ([conagrabrands.com](https://www.conagrabrands.com/files/events/2025-12-19/Q2FY26-Earnings-Press-Release))

Investments set equal to the carrying value of Conagra’s equity method investments (approx. $936.8M at FY2025) as the DCF bridge 'investments' input. ([conagrabrands.com](https://www.conagrabrands.com/files/2025-annual-report))

NOL balance equals approximately $25.6M foreign + $34.2M federal net operating loss carryforwards (modeled as $59.8M total) and NOL_utilization_pct is assumed (0.80) due to limited disclosure on full utilization schedule. ([conagrabrands.com](https://www.conagrabrands.com/files/2025-annual-report))

Comps: EV/NTM Revenue and EV/NTM EBITDA are proxied using StockAnalysis EV/Sales and EV/EBITDA, and P/E NTM is proxied using StockAnalysis 'Forward PE'. Treat as directional reasonableness checks rather than precise NTM consensus metrics. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/khc/statistics/))

catalysts: Sustained margin recovery (cost savings/productivity) that supports moving adjusted operating margin toward the top end of guidance.
Deleveraging trajectory and free-cash-flow conversion improvements that reduce equity discount risk.
company_overview: Conagra Brands is a U.S.-centric branded food company with operations across Grocery & Snacks, Refrigerated & Frozen, International, and Foodservice.
FY2025 net sales were $11.6B, with operating profit heavily influenced by non-cash impairment charges in certain years.
Strategy emphasizes brand-building and disciplined cost/cash-flow management while navigating macro/input cost volatility.
current_context: In Q2 FY26, reported net sales declined 6.8% and organic net sales declined 3.0%; reported operating margin was negative due to non-cash impairment charges, while adjusted operating margin was 11.3%.
FY2026 guidance (reaffirmed) calls for organic net sales change of (1)% to 1% and adjusted operating margin of ~11.0% to ~11.5%, alongside adjusted EPS of $1.70 to $1.85.
Company ended the quarter with net debt of $7.6B (3.83x net leverage).
investment_highlights: Base case assumes flat-to-low single-digit revenue growth consistent with management’s organic sales range, with gradual normalization of profitability toward a 12.0% EBIT margin.
D&A and capex are modeled as roughly steady percentages of sales based on recent historical intensity.
Working-capital intensity is normalized from an unusually high recent peak toward a ~4.5%–5.0% of sales range, supporting free-cash-flow durability.
Valuation framework blends DCF outputs with peer EV/EBITDA and EV/Sales context (using forward PE and EV multiples from public market data providers).
key_risks: Further goodwill/brand impairments or other non-cash charges could distort GAAP operating profit and reduce investor confidence in earnings power.
Demand softness, retailer ordering volatility, and/or persistent cost-of-goods inflation could pressure organic growth and margins.

valuation_summary: The DCF base case anchors near-term margins to FY2026 adjusted operating margin guidance and transitions to a steady-state EBIT margin by year 5.
Terminal assumptions (Gordon growth) use economically conservative long-run growth and a separate WACC assumption for risk capture.
Peer comps are used as a reasonableness check rather than as the primary valuation driver, given differences in impairment/accounting and capital structure.
